question.text: In a futures contract, the exchange decides all contract terms EXCEPT:

explanation.text: The Logic: Futures contracts are standardized by the exchange, which decides terms such as the underlying asset, lot size, expiry date and tick size. The only term left to the buyer and seller is price, which is discovered through free interaction on the trading platform. The Trap: Lot size and expiry date are set by the exchange, unlike OTC forwards where every term is negotiable. Note: This standardization (with only price negotiated) is the defining contrast between exchange-traded futures and bilateral forwards.
